messages.subject: Multiple observations
parts:
Hello,

I have RT data on 20 consecutive timepoints, and want to analyse their growth curve (data is in wide format so each time point has its own column, here RT1:RT20). In the following code, I understand the assumption to be that each row corresponds to 1 participant, therefore I do not have to include a participant variable. However, each participant actually completed 10 trials (with 20 time points each), so in reality each participant has 10 rows. Is it possible to add trials to the code to integrate the repeated observations?
Additionally, in the future I want to present different participants with different trials, so would it be possible to incorporate nesting of trials within participants?

myModel <- '
# Growth curve
I =~ 1*RT1 + 1*RT2 + 1*RT3 + 1*RT4 + 1*RT5 + 1*RT6 + 1*RT7 + 1*RT8 + 1*RT9 + 1*RT10 + 1*RT11 + 1*RT12 + 1*RT13 + 1*RT14 + 1*RT15 + 1*RT16 + 1*RT17 + 1*RT18 + 1*RT19 + 1*RT20
L =~ 0*RT1 + 1*RT2 + 2*RT3 + 3*RT4 + 4*RT5 + 5*RT6 + 6*RT7 + 7*RT8 + 8*RT9 + 9*RT10 + 10*RT11 + 11*RT12 + 12*RT13 + 13*RT14 + 14*RT15 + 15*RT16 + 16*RT17 + 17*RT18 + 18*RT19 + 19*RT20
'

fit <- cfa(model = myModel, data = Datawide)
summary(fit)

The alternative is that lme4 will possibly suit my data better but I find lavaan a bit clearer, so wanted to ask for a second opinion before I switch.

Thank you,
Agata
